about: Per-language definitions for the structure rules; each language reads its extensions from the convention pack its source names. Each value names its published source; a rule a language cannot use is listed under not_applicable with its reason. A language with no measured cutoff for a scored rule does not run that rule until one is measured (docs/structure-languages.md).

python.module: dotted path under structure.import_direction.source_root, prefixed by import_direction.package
python.edges: import and from-import statements, relative levels resolved against the importer's package

typescript.edges: static import and export-from specifiers, import() and require() with a string literal or a template literal without substitutions; relative specifiers resolve against the importer's folder, then tsconfig compilerOptions.paths and baseUrl from the nearest tsconfig.json; a specifier tries the file, the TypeScript source for a .js specifier, the listed extensions and index files; bare package specifiers are third-party and ignored; type-only imports count

go.module: the package: one folder; its import path is the go.mod module path plus the folder relative to go.mod
go.edges: import specs whose path starts with the module path; _test.go files are not part of the graph
go.note: The compiler already rejects import cycles and enforces internal/ visibility; it allows sibling imports, so sibling-isolation and tier direction still apply.

typescript.code_folder: nearest folder holding TypeScript or JavaScript source
exempt: a data file a source file in the same folder imports by a relative specifier (a JSON module is part of the code)
tooling fixed files (package.json, tsconfig*.json and the other tooling-pack names)
a file a //go:embed pattern in a .go file of the same package matches (embed patterns may not leave the package folder)
files under testdata/, which the go tool ignores

python.top_tier: the package root and the folders directly under it

typescript.entry: files a package.json bin or main field names, when Git tracks them
typescript.top_tier: the folder holding that package.json and the folders directly under it

go.entry: a non-test file declaring package main, except files constrained by //go:build ignore
go.top_tier: the module root, or cmd/<name>/ directly under it

STRUCT.overlapping-responsibilities.unit: source files of one language directly in one folder; units of different languages are never compared

python.definitions: top-level functions and classes, and the methods of top-level classes; docstrings and comments removed

typescript.definitions: top-level function and class declarations, methods of top-level classes, and top-level const or let declarations whose value is an arrow function or function expression, exported or not; comments removed
typescript.source: not yet measured: the rule does not run for TypeScript

go.definitions: top-level function and method declarations; comments removed
go.source: not yet measured: the rule does not run for Go

typescript.members: sibling TypeScript or JavaScript source files; stems split at _, -, . and lower-to-upper case boundaries
typescript.domain_word_sources: comments and class, interface and type alias names
typescript.source: not yet measured: the rule does not run for TypeScript

python.identifiers: bound names at module and class level: functions, classes and assignment, for, with, walrus, type-alias, except-handler and match-as targets; imports and the names functions, lambdas and comprehensions bind excluded

typescript.identifiers: declared names at top level: functions, classes with their methods and fields, interfaces with their members, enums with their members, type aliases with the members of an object type, namespaces, and every name a variable declaration binds (destructuring included); imports excluded

go.identifiers: declared names at package level: the package clause, functions, methods, types with their struct fields and interface methods, constants and variables; imports excluded

RENAME.residue.source: a rename retires the old name in every language file; a name's words split at underscores, case changes and digit runs (guardrails/foundation/source/names.py); no cutoff

go.reason: A Go folder is a package. Moving prefixed files into a folder named for the concept creates a new package, which changes identifier visibility and import paths: a design change, not a placement fix. Go keeps related files in one package, often with a shared prefix.

shell.reason: Shell scripts have no packages, imports or definitions the rules read.

proposers.reason: The candidate proposers (kind-candidates, consumer-candidates, name-pairs) propose only for these languages: the judgments they feed (technical_kind_grouping, consumer_placement, same_thing) were measured on Python cases, so TypeScript and Go proposals wait for labelled TypeScript and Go cases. name-pairs reads TypeScript and Go definitions through the shared readers; kind-candidates and consumer-candidates read Python only.
